Design the fix for this requirement in the Apache ECharts repo at /workspace:

title: 'fix(axis): fix bar bandWidth with inversed time axis'
Context: Bar charts on an inversed time axis can calculate the wrong `bandWidth`, causing distorted bar sizing/spacing.
Desired outcome: Correct bar bandwidth calculation for inversed time axes so bar width matches the actual axis interval direction and rendered bars keep sensible spacing.
Acceptance: Bars on an inversed time axis render with the expected width; reversing the axis no longer distorts band sizing; non-inversed time-axis bar charts keep their current layout.

## Where to look
- `/workspace/src/layout/barGrid.ts`: `getValueAxesMinGaps()` and `makeColumnLayout()` (around lines 150-250). `getValueAxesMinGaps` computes the minimum gap between adjacent data values per value/time axis; `makeColumnLayout` turns it into bandWidth via `extentSpan / scaleSpan * minGap`.
- Read `getValueAxesMinGaps` VERY carefully. It sorts values and computes min diff. Look for how it collects values (`data.getStore().get(dimIdx, i)` or similar), whether it SORTS them, and how it handles the axis being inversed.
- The likely root cause: `getValueAxesMinGaps` iterates data in data order and computes `values[i] - values[i-1]` WITHOUT sorting (or sorts but then the diff can be negative / zero when inversed), or it early-returns on a non-positive gap. Determine the ACTUAL mechanism by reading the code.
- Also check `src/layout/barPolar.ts` for the analogous path, and whether `axis.inverse` / `axis.isBlank` / `scale.getExtent()` ordering matters. Note `makeColumnLayout` already uses `Math.abs()` for extentSpan and scaleSpan.
- Check whether the bug is instead in the `min`/`max` tracking loop skipping duplicate/unsorted values, or in `Math.abs` being missing on the per-pair diff.

## Also determine
- Whether `getValueAxesMinGaps` needs `Math.abs` on the gap, or a sort, or a fix to its `lastValue`/`min` initialization.
- Whether a unit test can be written under `/workspace/test/ut/spec/layout/` (check existing tests there and in test/ut/spec/ for barGrid/barLayout tests) that asserts bar width equality between inverse:true and inverse:false time axes. Look at how existing tests build charts (`createChart` helper in test/ut/core/utHelper.ts) and read the layout result (e.g. `series.getData().getItemLayout(0).width`).

Produce a precise implementation plan with exact anchors. Do NOT modify any file — this is design only. Verify with `git status --short` that you left the repo unchanged.

input.rootCause:
The bug is NOT in `getValueAxesMinGaps()`/`makeColumnLayout()` in `/workspace/src/layout/barGrid.ts` — that code already sorts the collected values ascending, ignores non-positive deltas (`if (delta > 0)`), and already wraps both `extentSpan` and `scaleSpan` in `Math.abs()`, so it is orientation-agnostic. `src/layout/barPolar.ts` also already uses `Math.abs(axisExtent[1] - axisExtent[0])`, and `Axis.getBandWidth()` is abs-safe too.

The real culprit is `adjustScaleForOverflow()` in `/workspace/src/coord/axisHelper.ts` (line 118):

    const axisExtent = model.axis.getExtent();
    const axisLength = axisExtent[1] - axisExtent[0];   // NEGATIVE when axis.inverse === true

`Grid.adjustAxes()` (`/workspace/src/coord/cartesian/Grid.ts:219`) sets the pixel extent reversed for an inversed axis (`axis.setExtent(extent[1], extent[0])`), so `getExtent()` returns e.g. `[500, 0]` and `axisLength` becomes `-500`. `adjustScaleForOverflow()` then computes

    oldRangePercentOfNew = 1 - (minOverflow + maxOverflow) / axisLength;   // > 1 instead of < 1
    overflowBuffer = oldRange / oldRangePercentOfNew - oldRange;            // NEGATIVE instead of positive

so instead of *expanding* the time scale extent to make room for the half-bars sticking out past the first/last data point, it *shrinks* it. Since `makeColumnLayout()` derives `bandWidth = extentSpan / scaleSpan * minGap` from `baseAxis.scale.getExtent()` (which by layout time is the niced, wrongly-shrunk extent), a smaller `scaleSpan` inflates `bandWidth`.

Measured empirically (500x400 chart, zero grid padding, `xAxis: {type:'time'}`, 3 daily points, one bar series; I patched, ran, and reverted):
- inverse:false → scale span 263,816,793 ms, bandWidth 163.75, bar width 112.9875, item0 x=29.76 (right edge 142.7, inside grid)
- inverse:true (buggy) → scale span 128,475,836 ms (SMALLER than the raw 172,800,000 ms data span, so the first/last points fall outside the scale), bandWidth 336.25 (2.05x too big), bar width 232.01, item0 x=470.24 → right edge 702.3, i.e. 202 px outside the 500 px grid. That is exactly the "distorted bar sizing/spacing" symptom.
- inverse:true with `Math.abs()` applied → scale span, bandWidth (163.75), and bar width (112.9875) become bit-identical to the non-inversed case, and item0 x=357.26 is the exact mirror (500 - 29.76 - 112.99).

Note the min/max buffer split (`maxOverflow / totalOverFlow`) needs no inverse-aware swap: `doCalBarWidthAndOffset()` always lays offsets out symmetrically about 0 (first offset `-widthSum/2`, last `offset+width = +widthSum/2`), so `minOverflow === maxOverflow` and the distribution is symmetric regardless of direction.
input.upstreamApproach: Almost certainly a one-line `Math.abs()` on the axis length inside `adjustScaleForOverflow` in `src/coord/axisHelper.ts` (mirroring the `Math.abs()` guards that already exist in `barGrid.makeColumnLayout`, `barPolar.calRadialBar` and `Axis.getBandWidth`), plus a unit test asserting the bar/band width is identical for `inverse: true` and `inverse: false` time axes. The commit title says "fix(axis)" rather than "fix(bar)", consistent with the change landing in the axis/scale-extent helper rather than in the bar layout.

plan.rationale: This is the single orientation-dependent expression in the whole bar-bandWidth path. `Math.abs` is a no-op for non-inversed axes (extent[1] > extent[0]), so existing layouts are bit-for-bit unchanged, while inversed time axes now get the same scale expansion (and therefore the same scaleSpan and bandWidth) as non-inversed ones.

Locks the acceptance criteria: equal band/bar width across inverse:true/false, no distortion, and no grid overflow. Both assertions fail on the unfixed code and pass with the one-line change, and the mirroring assertion also guards against a future 'fix' that merely clamps the width without restoring the scale extent.

This file is the one explicitly referenced by the FIXME comment above `adjustScaleForOverflow`'s call site (`// See #6728, #4862, test/bar-overflow-time-plot.html`). Skip if you prefer to keep the diff minimal.

testPlan: Run the new spec only: `cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false test/ut/spec/chart/bar/barBandWidthInverseTimeAxis.test.ts` — expect 2 passing tests.

Sanity-check the test actually catches the bug: stash the axisHelper.ts change (`git stash push src/coord/axisHelper.ts`), re-run the spec and confirm both assertions fail (bandWidth 336.25 vs 163.75; x0+width = 702.3 > 500), then restore.

Run the whole unit suite: `npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false`. Baseline on this working tree already has 3 failing suites from other in-flight work (test/ut/spec/chart/map/regionSilent.test.ts, test/ut/spec/component/geo/regionSilent.test.ts, test/ut/spec/coord/axisTicksInsideExtent.test.ts). I verified these 3 fail identically with and without the axisHelper patch — no new failures are introduced. Existing bar/candlestick/boxplot/BarView specs all pass.

Non-regression proof for non-inversed axes: `Math.abs` is the identity when extent[1] > extent[0], so `test/bar-overflow-time-plot.html`, `test/bar2.html`, `test/bar-large.html` render identically; optionally confirm via the visual test server (`npm run test:visual`) on bar-overflow-time-plot.html.

Manual check in test/bar-overflow-time-plot.html with `inverse: true` added to a time xAxis: bars should be mirrored, evenly spaced, of the same width as the non-inversed chart, and fully inside the grid.
risks: The fix changes the niced scale extent (and therefore tick/label positions and dataZoom ranges) for any chart that combines a bar series with an inversed time base axis. That is the intended correction, but any stored visual-regression baseline containing that combination will legitimately change. No such case exists in test/ util specs today.

`adjustScaleForOverflow` still divides by `axisLength`, which is 0 before the grid has been resized (`Axis._extent` starts at [0, 0]); the result is ±Infinity and then a degenerate buffer. `Math.abs` does not introduce this, but it also does not fix it. If you want belt-and-braces, add an early `if (!(axisLength > 0)) { return {min: min, max: max}; }` — flag it as a separate concern rather than folding it in silently, since it could alter behavior in unusual init orders.

Do NOT 'fix' this in src/layout/barGrid.ts: `getValueAxesMinGaps` already sorts ascending and filters `delta > 0`, and `makeColumnLayout` already abs-es both spans. Adding a redundant Math.abs/sort there would look like a fix while the scale extent stays wrong, and the mirroring/overflow assertions in the new test would still fail.

Assertion tolerance: bandWidth/width values carry floating-point noise (e.g. 112.98750000002714), so compare with toBeCloseTo, not toBe, and give the grid explicit zero padding so the numbers do not depend on default label sizing in jsdom.
